name: Ahaz
overview: Ahaz was a male king from the tribe of Judah, noted as the son of Jotham. He ruled as King of Judah but did not follow the righteous ways of David, his forefather, failing to do what was right in the sight of the LORD. His reign is marked by spiritual decline and disobedience to God.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Ahaz' means 'he has grasped,' reflecting a proper Hebrew name. His titles, including 'King Ahaz' and 'King of Judah,' identify his royal status but do not carry a divine origin or special meaning beyond his position as monarch.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ahaz as the son of Jotham. It is also inferred that he was the father of Hezekiah and Maaseiah, indicating his place within the Davidic lineage and the royal succession of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Ahaz is significant in the biblical narrative as a king who exemplified spiritual apostasy by engaging in idolatry and abandoning the faithful practices of his ancestors. His reliance on foreign powers rather than trusting God led to political and spiritual consequences for Judah. His actions, including desecrating the temple and adopting pagan practices, serve as a cautionary example of unfaithfulness and the dangers of forsaking God's covenant.
